Paragraph:
Translation: My intelligence is bewildered by Your equivocal instructions. Therefore, please tell me decisively what is most beneficial for me.

Purport (Excerpt): In the previous chapter... many different paths were explained... This was all presented unsystematically. A more organized outline of the path would be necessary for action and understanding. Arjuna, therefore, wanted to clear up these apparently confusing matters...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Overwhelm caused by processing complex, seemingly paradoxical instructions without a singular, clear directive.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna openly admits his bewilderment and requests a single, decisive path (ekam vadatya niscitya) that will bring ultimate benefit.
Outcome/Resolution: By acknowledging his mental confusion, Arjuna opens the door for Krishna to deliver a structured breakdown of Karma-yoga.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Overcoming Choice Paralysis: Resolving mental freeze caused by seemingly conflicting options
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Communicating Confusion: Vocalizing intellectual overwhelm directly without shame
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Desire for Decisiveness: Seeking a clear, actionable directive to move forward

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sreyas (Ultimate long-term benefit vs. immediate preference)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna feels his intellect is clouded by what seems like conflicting advice between meditative knowledge and active duty. He asks Krishna to cut through the complexity and prescribe the single most beneficial path (Sreyas) for his spiritual progress.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: When faced with too many choices or complex theories, the human mind suffers from decision fatigue and paralysis. Arjuna demonstrates healthy self-advocacy by pausing, admitting he is overwhelmed, and asking for a practical, clear prioritization strategy to guide his next steps.
